stem.en: In the classification hierarchy, which group, class or genus, has fewer members but more features in common?

text.en: Genus, as it is a lower level inside a class.

feedback.en: Right. At each lower level there are fewer members, and they share more common features.

text.en: Class, because a higher level always has fewer members.

feedback.en: A class holds many genera, so it has more members than any one of them.

text.en: Class, because members of a large group share the most.

feedback.en: A large group holds very different members, so they share fewer features.

text.en: Neither, because all levels hold the same number of members.

feedback.en: The number of members falls at each lower level.

explanation.en: At each lower level, organisms share more common features, and every lower group is a part of the group above it. So a genus has fewer members than the class it sits in, and more in common.

hints.en: Which of the two sits lower in the address?
